nodes.statement: The apparent rigidity of the probe response is an artifact of the specific chemical stoichiometry (Ca/Si/Al/O ratio) used in the simulation; introducing controlled doping or alloying into the lattice introduces localized electronic states that modify the effective potential landscape, thereby altering the probe's perceived rigidity through charge transfer and bond polarization effects.

The solution space appears rigid because the simulation model employs a perfect crystal lattice without accounting for intrinsic defects such as vacancies or dislocations; the presence of these defects creates localized soft modes and strain fields that would be detected by a sensitive probe, revealing a fundamentally flexible solution space that is masked in idealized models.
